text: Human surface, phases 001-activity-and-actor and 002-routine-layer: which reference files implement an activity feed, an inbox, an actor on a record and routines with an until outcome, what should the builder lift or mirror, and which failures or fixes in those repos does the plan not guard against?

Trust, phases 006-approval-grants, 007-per-bot-apps and 008-vault: which reference files implement approval grants, per-bot tool or app filtering and a secret store with injection, what should the builder lift or mirror, and which leak, bypass or precedence bugs did those repos hit that the plan does not guard against?

openhuman-full, never studied before: what do its five vendored crates (tinyagents, tinyconnectors, tinymemory, tinyhumans-sdk, tinysecurity) and its built openhuman-tui crate hold that openhuman-main lacks, and what does that change for phase 003-terminal-screen and its six children and for any other planned phase?

Phase 011-messaging-channels: which reference files implement a channel adapter seam, Telegram, Slack, Signal and WhatsApp transports, identity linking, a durable queue and approvals rendered as buttons or replies, what should the builder lift or mirror, and which delivery, retry or duplicate-message failures did those repos hit?

Prompt and records, phases 004-computer-exposure, 005-memory, 009-skills and 010-conversations: which reference files implement a working place named in the prompt, shared and per-bot memory with a size bound, a skill list under a cap and an append-only conversation with bot routing, and which pitfalls did those repos hit?

Net-new and operations: what do the ten reference repos have that neither the 003 build plan nor the skip list of the parity synthesis covers, ranked by value to a small team, and which test corpora, failure-handling patterns and upgrade paths in those repos should feed phases 012-manual-testing-scenarios, 013-skilled-and-doc-alignment and 014-deep-review?
